title: KIST Connects South Korean Quantum Startups to Midwest Ecosystem Across Wisconsin and Chicago - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Following Quantum World Congress (QWC) 2026, four South Korean quantum startups expanded their U.S. commercial strategy through the Global Bridge Program across Wisconsin and Illinois. Spearheaded by the Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST), the delegation engaged with venture accelerators, research institutions, economic development boards, and hard-tech manufacturing hubs to establish cross-border technology partnerships and market entry pathways.

The initiative forms part of South Korea’s Deeptech Incubator Project for Startups (DIPS), overseen by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and administered by the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, with KIST directing the quantum technology domain. In Milwaukee, the delegation conducted pitch sessions with venture platform gener8tor and met with the Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation (WEDC) to prepare for an official Wisconsin trade delegation visit to South Korea.

In Chicago, the delegation met with ecosystem leaders at the Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE), the Bloch Quantum Tech Hub, hard-tech innovation center mHUB, and the 128-acre Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP). Startup executives presented their technical frameworks to Dr. David Awschalom, Founding Director of the CQE, while coordinating with the Illinois Economic Development Corporation to leverage regional microelectronics packaging and manufacturing infrastructure.
